hypotheses.reasoning: POST /v1/notify 503s at the gateway (e.g. #3685, #5041) are downstream symptoms. The origin is template-svc: its last log line is #3561 at 12:00:48 (a routine GC pause, heap 40%), and after that it emits nothing for the rest of the incident. Eight seconds later, at #3580 (12:00:56), notification-svc gets ECONNREFUSED from template-svc at 10.25.98.71:8081, and every later render fails the same way (#3699, #3831, #4015). Notification-svc does not reach template-svc, so the notify path fails fast, not by hanging, which points to the process dying rather than a slow dependency. There is no FATAL or restart line to confirm the cause. The heap at 40% makes a plain OOM less likely, so the exact crash mechanism is unverified. Separate fault, not on the notify path: accounts-db filled its disk (WARN #2895 at 95% at 11:57:58, #3636 at 99% at 12:01:20, then 'No space left on device' #3948, #4145). That causes account-svc DiskFullError and the /login 500s (#3977, #4256, #3959), and is not the cause of the notify outage.

Alternative reading: template-svc became unreachable from the network side (not a process crash), which would make this a dependency outage. The connection-refused errors fit a dead listener better than a hung dependency, so this is less likely.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1) Restart template-svc now and confirm it is listening on 10.25.98.71:8081, then check its pod/container exit reason (OOM kill, panic, or node eviction) and its last stderr, since the service logged nothing before it went silent at 12:00:48. 2) Separately, free space on accounts-db's data volume (/var/lib/postgresql/data, WAL/binlog growth ~560MB/h): purge or archive WAL/binlogs, expand the volume, and confirm inserts succeed. This restores /login and signup, but it is a separate fault from the notify outage. 3) Add a liveness alert on template-svc and a disk-usage alert on accounts-db at 80%.

hypotheses.reasoning: POST /v1/notify 503s at the gateway (e.g. #3685, #5041) are downstream symptoms. The origin is template-svc: its last log line is #3561 at 12:00:48 (a routine GC pause, heap 40%), and after that it emits nothing for the rest of the incident. Eight seconds later, at #3580 (12:00:56), notification-svc gets ECONNREFUSED from template-svc at 10.25.98.71:8081, and every later render fails the same way (#3699, #3831, #4015). Notification-svc does not reach template-svc, so the notify path fails fast, not by hanging, which points to the process dying rather than a slow dependency. There is no FATAL or restart line to confirm the cause. The heap at 40% makes a plain OOM less likely, so the exact crash mechanism is unverified. Separate fault, not on the notify path: accounts-db filled its disk (WARN #2895 at 95% at 11:57:58, #3636 at 99% at 12:01:20, then 'No space left on device' #3948, #4145). That causes account-svc DiskFullError and the /login 500s (#3977, #4256, #3959), and is not the cause of the notify outage.

Alternative reading: template-svc became unreachable from the network side (not a process crash), which would make this a dependency outage. The connection-refused errors fit a dead listener better than a hung dependency, so this is less likely.

input.recommendedAction: 1) Restart template-svc now and confirm it is listening on 10.25.98.71:8081, then check its pod/container exit reason (OOM kill, panic, or node eviction) and its last stderr, since the service logged nothing before it went silent at 12:00:48. 2) Separately, free space on accounts-db's data volume (/var/lib/postgresql/data, WAL/binlog growth ~560MB/h): purge or archive WAL/binlogs, expand the volume, and confirm inserts succeed. This restores /login and signup, but it is a separate fault from the notify outage. 3) Add a liveness alert on template-svc and a disk-usage alert on accounts-db at 80%.
